extra.message: SQL Injection in /select via username parameter — Full read access to the users table (names, addresses, emails, MD5 password hashes) via UNION/boolean-based SQLi; potential further exploitation via SQLite functions. [verified: username is spliced unparameterized into the SQL string with no validation anywhere in the request path.]

SQL Injection in DELETE /user via user.address field — Attacker-controlled destructive SQL statement execution (delete arbitrary rows, or chain further statements depending on driver support). [verified: user.address is interpolated unquoted into a DELETE statement, confirmed at main.py:235 with no sanitization.]

Missing authentication on all endpoints including destructive /reset — Any anonymous user can wipe and rebuild the entire SQL and NoSQL databases (DoS/data loss) by issuing POST /reset. [verified: No auth dependency/middleware exists anywhere in main.py; POST /reset destroys and rebuilds both databases unauthenticated.]

Sensitive data exposure of password hashes and PII via /select — Unauthenticated attacker obtains full PII and password hashes for all users, especially when combined with the SQLi in /select. [verified: run_sql_query's bulk-row path returns raw tuples including the password column, unlike the single-row path which strips fields, so SQLi/bulk /select dumps expose password hashes and PII unauthenticated.]

NoSQL query injection in POST /find — Attacker can craft arbitrary Mongo-style query operators (e.g. $ne, $regex) to bypass intended filtering and enumerate/extract all user records including data outside intended scope. [verified: Raw JSON body is passed straight to MontyDB find() as the query filter with no schema or operator restriction.]

Insecure password hashing using unsalted MD5 — Any leaked password hash (e.g. via SQLi in /select) can be cracked quickly, exposing plaintext user passwords, likely reused elsewhere. [verified: Password hashed via plain md5() with no salt, confirmed at main.py:187.]

Unauthenticated PII disclosure via GET /find — Any unauthenticated attacker can enumerate and read PII for arbitrary users via the NoSQL-backed /find endpoint [verified: GET /find passes raw username into get_nosql_users which returns full PII (minus password) with no auth or ownership check, confirming unauthenticated PII disclosure on the NoSQL path.]
